messages:
mira: Customer hit intermittent 502s and long tail latency on SSE stream from a Windows laptop behind a corporate proxy. They sent `request_id=req_9a8b7c6d`. Said it works fine from macOS.

jordan: thx mira. can you paste the minimal curl they used? also which curl version on win?

mira: they used Windows 10, curl 7.75 via Git for Windows, PowerShell. This is the minimal repro they shared:
```
curl.exe -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-4x"
```

mira: behavior: stream starts, a few SSE events then connection resets with 502 from our edge. Sometimes long pause (~20s) then resumed, sometimes hard cut.

support-bot: Automated note: matched req_9a8b7c6d to edge node eu-west-1-edge-13. Logs show: ``504 upstream read timeout`` at 2024-10-03T15:12:41Z and a follow-up 502 from proxy.

alex: can we confirm whether proxy is doing chunked encoding translation or TLS interception? windows+corporate proxies often alter `Connection` or chunk headers. ask customer for proxy type + any auth (NTLM/Negotiate).

mira: customer says corporate proxy w/ NTLM. they can reproduce without proxy on personal hotspot. so likely proxy interaction.

ryan-ops: steps to gather a useful debug bundle: 1) reproducible curl command (with --trace-ascii) 2) curl --version output 3) PowerShell exact command (escaping differs) 4) full response headers (raw) 5) redwood support wants edge request ID and server logs (we have req_9a8b7c6d) 6) packet capture (if allowed).

jordan: give them a minimal tracing command for Windows PowerShell to capture full TLS/HTTP handshake and streaming events:
```
# PowerShell (escape double quotes)
curl.exe -N -v --trace-ascii trace.txt -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-4x" 2>curl_v.txt
# Attach trace.txt and curl_v.txt to the case.
```

alex: also ask them to try curl with HTTP/1.1 (some corporate proxies mess http2 multiplexing): `curl.exe -N --http1.1 -H ...` and with `--no-keepalive` vs `--keepalive-time 0` to see differences.

mira: posted that to customer and asked for: proxy vendor/name/version, NTLM vs basic, the two traces, and whether reproduces from home hotspot.

support-bot: Checklist added to ticket: [trace attached], [edge logs correlated], [proxy vendor], [pcap if allowed], [curl versions].

jordan: one extra troubleshooting tip: on Win Git-curl there is a libcurl build that enables `schannel` which can cause shorter TLS renegotiation windows. If they can try curl from WSL (Ubuntu) that isolates Windows-specific TLS stack. ask them to try WSL curl too.

ryan-ops: if they can't capture pcap, ask proxy admin to provide proxy logs for the time window. we want to see any `RST` from proxy to our edge or `502` generated by intermediate.

mira: customer returned with traces. trace shows `HTTP/2 200` initial headers then a `GOAWAY` from proxy followed by `RST_STREAM`. attaching snippets:```
<< recv frame HEADERS (status 200)
data: event: message
...
<< recv frame GOAWAY (error_code=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM, last_stream_id=17)
<< recv frame RST_STREAM (stream_id=9, error=REFUSED_STREAM)
```

alex: ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM is often seen when proxy has rate/stream limits. suggest they try single-stream test (no parallel streams) and set `--no-buffer` so curl doesn't open extra pipelines. also ask proxy team to increase stream window or disable stream concurrency for that client.

mira: forwarded recommendation to proxy admin and asked them to try WSL curl. waiting on their response.

jordan: good. once they provide proxy logs we'll correlate with our edge timestamp 2024-10-03T15:12:41Z for req_9a8b7c6d. if proxy confirms RST/GOAWAY we can classify as "intermediate proxy stream termination" and advise two mitigations: 1) use a client that supports long single HTTP/1.1 SSE stream or 2) adjust proxy config.

mira: closing loop: customer tried WSL curl -> stable stream. proxy admin increased concurrent stream limit -> stable. customer confirmed fix. marking ticket resolved and documenting troubleshooting steps for future Win+NTLM cases. :tada:
